name: Soraya
description: Earth-born heir of the dragonkin tribe. About a century old but appearing Tomas's peer (late 20s-30s) -- young by her people's reckoning, already older than any human he has known, and carrying a gravity beyond her apparent years. Her scales are earthy browns and burnt oranges, brilliant and luminous with the strength of an exceptional gift; draconic eyes, ridged brow, and the bound wings all dragonkin bear, which she can mantle as a shield. Strong of body and of will. Steady, patient, reserved; the bearing of someone raised to lead a grieving people and to give nothing away, least of all to the man sent to drive them out.
abilities: Exceptionally gifted for her kind -- her scales burn bright with it. A master shielder (stone walls, raised cover, unbreakable defense); the land's strength (immense, immovable physical power); and the deep-sense of the ground (she reads footfalls, distant movement, and the health of the land, and feels the Ashing begin before any other). Uniquely among earth-kin, she can wake living green from bare ground -- tender growth that flourishes briefly before the Ashing withers it. Her gift and her curse in one image: she makes life, and her staying unmakes it.
backstory: Daughter and heir to the tribe-leader (her father), raised to inherit the hardest burden her people carry: to hold a cursed, homeless nation together and lead it, generation after generation, down the endless road. She was an infant when the curse fell and the homeland was lost, carried into exile in her father's arms; she has no memory of life as anything but wandering, and has never known a home. What she knows of it comes from her father's stories of their lost homeland -- the progenitor's seat, a city of grandeur their people built with their own talents, now buried beneath the desert their own curse made. Her mother died in that first Ashing, clinging to the dying home -- so, without her knowing it, Soraya's own longing to stay is the echo of her mother's. Those stories woke in her a longing her wandering life could never answer. Once, against her father's will, she refused to move on: she found a place she loved and stayed behind, desperate to make it home. She watched it die. The Ashing crept out from her staying and slowly poisoned the land and the innocents already living there, until the home she wanted was another wasteland and its people were ruined. That is the wound beneath her discipline -- she learned, in the cruelest way, that for her to want a home is to destroy it, and to harm the innocent who share it. She has wanted nothing she cannot carry ever since. When the human knight is left among them as guarantor, keeping watch over the collateral falls to her as heir; she resents the crown he serves, does the duty coldly and correctly, and is slowly, unwillingly disarmed by the man beneath the title.
theBonding: She and Tomas are soul-bonded by the marriage rite. During it the three aspects of the triune god -- Father, Mother, Child -- question her, and she must answer each truthfully; the god acknowledges her people's curse, blesses the couple and their coming hardships, and warns that a disaster approaches. Through the bond she gains a share of Tomas's faith-channel -- the power to channel divinity into armaments, a startling gift for one whose curse forbids her instruments of conflict -- and shares his senses and skills, as he shares her earth. The bond is damaged by the progenitor-spirit's assault on Tomas, so the shared-death rule is broken: rather than dying together, the death of one leaves the other catastrophically, permanently wounded. In the end it is Soraya who falls to the hyenadin, and Tomas who is left maimed among the ash.
motivation: WANT: fulfill her duty -- secure the crown's resources, lead her people safely onward, hold the tribe together on the road. NEED: to be allowed to want -- a home, permanence, something she can keep -- and to believe that her wanting need not destroy what she loves. She buried this longing after it killed a home once; Tomas reawakens it, and because she has already learned exactly what her love costs, she fears having him more than she fears losing him.
arc: From the cold, dutiful heir who wants nothing she cannot carry -- to a woman who lets herself want, at last, the one thing she swore she never would: Tomas, and the rooted home he embodies. When the war-summons forces his choice, she breaks the discipline of a lifetime and does the thing she has never done -- she asks him to stay. He refuses. Then the hyenadin fall on the mesa, and Soraya is killed defending her people, the last of the fold to fall -- dying without ever knowing he turned back. Through the damaged bond her death does not kill Tomas but maims him. Her lifelong dread is fulfilled to the letter: she let herself want, and the wanting ended in her death and his ruin.
traits: self-denying -- wants nothing she cannot carry
a buried, guilty longing for home
haunted by the home she once destroyed
slow to trust, slower to let go

relationships.Tomas (Ser Warrant): The human guarantor she is set to keep -- the face of her people's expulsion, who becomes the soul-mate whose bond-stone blazes for her when she clasps it. He reawakens the longing she buried; she, uniquely, already knows what having him would cost him. In the end she breaks her silence to ask him to stay; he refuses and leaves, and she is killed before he turns back -- dying never knowing that he did.
relationships.Kaelen, her father: The tribe-leader she is bound to succeed, who raised her alone on the road and woke her longing with stories of the home he keeps. They once clashed over her staying behind; the grief of that failure sits between them, as does the knowledge that he was among the warmakers whose sin brought the curse and killed her mother. In their last moments, as the hyenadin overwhelm the fold, father and daughter reckon and forgive at last -- shown through her eyes before she falls.
relationships.Her people: Her charge and her burden; the reason she can never simply choose herself. A cursed, weary nation whose survival rests on the heir keeping faith.
relationships.The squire: The human who rides for the crown's resources; his return is the clock that ends her weeks with Tomas and forces every choice.

openQuestions: The lost homeland's name; where and when she stayed behind (and who was lost there); whether she knows the full extent of her father Kaelen's guilt in the war that brought the curse and killed her mother.
